content:
incident-bot: PagerDuty CRIT -> eu-west-2 networking: high error rate for private service discovery consumers. Incident created and paged to oncall sam.

sam: I'm on call — looking at alerts. Internal DNS (10.0.2.53) showing NXDOMAINs for *.service.internal and a spike of 502/504s from ingestion workers. Jobs failing to reach postgres endpoints.

maya: I can reproduce — curl to service.internal resolves to IPs that belong to a decommissioned VPC in a different AZ. Seems like private hosted zone got associated incorrectly. Any recent infra changes?

leo: That was my Terraform job 12m ago — I added a secondary CIDR and then ran a hosted zone association. I think I pointed the hosted zone at the old VPC by mistake. Command I ran:

```
aws route53 associate-vpc-with-hosted-zone \
  --hosted-zone-id Z0123456789 \
  --vpc VPCRegionA=vpc-old-123
```

I was rushed, apologies.

sam: Ok that explains cross-VPC resolution. When the private hosted zone is associated to vpc-old-123, clients in eu-west-2 keep resolving to IPs that have no working return path (we're seeing asymmetric routing to a retired NAT instance). Need fast rollback.

ova: Can someone confirm route tables / NAT status in vpc-old-123? I see the nat-instance there is status=stopped in the console, and the route table has 0.0.0.0/0 -> i-0deadbeef (the old NAT).

(ova pastes output)
```
$ aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-old-123 --query 'RouteTables[].Routes'
[
  {"DestinationCidrBlock": "0.0.0.0/0", "InstanceId": "i-0deadbeef", "State": "blackhole"},
  {"DestinationCidrBlock": "10.0.0.0/16", "VpcPeeringConnectionId": "pcx-12345"}
]
```

maya: Blackhole default route + wrong hosted zone = service names resolving to IPs behind dead NAT. Customers hit timeouts and fallbacks.

sam: Mitigation plan — quick steps:
1) Disassociate hosted zone from vpc-old-123 (stop wrong DNS answers)
2) Re-associate hosted zone to the intended VPC (vpc-eu-west-2b)
3) Confirm internal DNS TTL/flush and test resolution
4) If any east-west routing still broken, add temporary route to redirect traffic to working NAT/IGW or bring up standby NAT instance
5) Post status update and customer comms

carol: Support: roughly 50 active customer jobs failing, ~12% error rate on ingestion lane. Cataloging impacted tenants now. Will send an initial status page update once we have mitigation step 1 complete.

incident-bot: Suggested command: `aws route53 disassociate-vpc-from-hosted-zone --hosted-zone-id Z0123456789 --vpc VPCRegionA=vpc-old-123`

maya: Running disassociate now.

leo: I revoked the Terraform apply and set a lock in the workspace; no further changes.

sam: Disassociate succeeded. Confirmed via `get-hosted-zone` that vpc-old-123 is no longer in associations. Trying re-associate to vpc-eu-west-2b.

(leo pastes command he's about to run)
```
aws route53 associate-vpc-with-hosted-zone --hosted-zone-id Z0123456789 --vpc VPCRegionA=vpc-eu-west-2b
```

leo: Re-associate complete. Patched internal resolvers to flush caches (systemd-resolve --flush-caches).

maya: I'm seeing correct A records now returning private IPs in the expected subnet. Running quick smoke tests against postgres endpoints — connects succeed.

ova: We did have some lingering connections that hit the old NAT instance; I added a temporary 0.0.0.0/0 route in vpc-old-123 route table to point to the IGW so any stray traffic won't blackhole (this is short-lived remediation). Command: `aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-abc123 --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --gateway-id igw-123456`

sam: Good. Confirming system metrics: error rate down from 12% -> 1.8% in last 5m; job backlog draining.

carol: Support: notifying customers impacted that we’ve mitigated DNS misassociation and are monitoring. ETA for full recovery: 15-30m for all backfills.

kevin: Product note: this was a human error in infra change — suggest adding a pre-apply check for host-zone vpc-id matches intended environment and a Terraform plan guard. Also request a postmortem if we don't already have one.

sam: Agree. For now I'm handing off to leo for root cause and remediation follow-up. leo, can you own the RCA and runbook updates?

leo: On it. I'll capture the exact command diff and add a protective guard to the infra module. Will also propose an automated association verification test in CI.

maya: I'm going to close the incident when metrics are stable for 30m and customer backfills are at acceptable rates.

incident-bot: Incident status -> Mitigated. Severity -> degraded. Next steps: RCA owner=leo, postmortem due in 5 business days, followup runbook PR requested.

sam: Thanks everyone. Handoff to leo for RCA and to carol for customer follow-ups.

leo: Filing RCA draft and will ping for review.

carol: I'll send a final status update once the backlog is cleared. :white_check_mark:
